relationship_types.label: Direct Quranic Reference
relationship_types.definition: A relationship where a Topic or Dimension is explicitly grounded in one or more specific Quranic verses (ayahs). This is the primary evidentiary link between conceptual taxonomy and divine text.
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Connects abstract knowledge nodes to their textual source. Must be verifiable via verse key.

example.description: Topic 'Tawheed Fundamentals' is directly referenced by this ayah mapping.

relationship_types.label: Lexical Relation
relationship_types.definition: A relationship based on shared Arabic root (jizr), morphological form, or semantic field within Quranic vocabulary. Captures etymological and linguistic connections.
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Links concepts that share linguistic DNA (e.g., s-l-m linking salām, silm, islām). Critical for polysemy management.

example.description: Both derive from s-l-m root; polysemous relationship requires careful disambiguation.

relationship_types.label: Morphological Relation
relationship_types.definition: A specialized lexical relationship indicating derivation through specific Arabic verb forms (awzan) or noun patterns. Distinguishes between Form I, II, III, IV, etc., nuances.
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Captures causal, intensive, reciprocal, or reflexive nuances derived from form changes (e.g., ṣ-l-ḥ Form I vs Form IV).

example.description: Form IV (aṣlaḥa) derives from same root as Form I (ṣulḥ) but carries transitive/causative meaning.

relationship_types.label: Thematic Relation
relationship_types.definition: A conceptual relationship linking topics across different domains/dimensions based on shared thematic clusters or cross-cutting concerns (e.g., justice, mercy, covenant).
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Enables horizontal traversal across vertical taxonomy silos. Represents 'SHARES_CONCEPT' semantics from existing data.

example.description: Cross-cutting theme of Mizan/Wasat spans ethics, worship, economics, and environment.

relationship_types.label: Tafsir Supported
relationship_types.definition: A relationship validated or explained by classical/exegetical commentary. Indicates that the connection is not merely lexical or editorial but has scholarly interpretive backing.
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Adds weight to non-obvious connections. Essential for resolving ambiguity in polysemous terms or establishing historical context.

example.description: Concept of naskh is defined and bounded by tafsir literature; cannot be understood purely lexically.

relationship_types.label: Editorial Classification
relationship_types.definition: A structural relationship created by human curators or AI-assisted taxonomy builders to organize knowledge. Includes CONTAINS, PARENT_OF, and administrative groupings.
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Provides hierarchical scaffolding. Distinct from semantic relationships; purely organizational.

example.description: Domain contains dimension; structural containment, not semantic equivalence.

relationship_types.label: Contrast / Antonymy
relationship_types.definition: A relationship defining opposition, negation, or complementary duality between concepts (e.g., Tawheed vs Shirk, Sabr vs Haste).
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Critical for theological boundaries and ethical binaries. Helps define concepts via negation.

example.description: Fundamental theological antithesis; defining one requires understanding the other.

relationship_types.label: Contemporary Application
relationship_types.definition: Links foundational Quranic concepts to modern issues, technologies, or contexts. Bridges classical text with present-day relevance.
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Enables practical guidance extraction. Must be clearly distinguished from eternal principles to avoid anachronism.

example.description: Classical prohibition applied to contemporary financial instruments; requires fiqh methodology bridge.

relationship_types.label: Narrative Relation
relationship_types.definition: Links entities within prophetic stories, historical events, or parables. Captures chronological, causal, or character-based connections.
relationship_types.semantic_scope: Preserves story coherence separate from doctrinal extraction. Allows narrative traversal without conflating with legal/theological edges.

example.description: Prophet Musa's narrative arc is causally linked to Firawn's tyranny; inseparable in Quranic telling.
